title: Trade and International Business: Research & Analysis | CSIS
text:
Trade and International Business

Reciprocal tariffs, threats to global supply chains, and comparative manufacturing advantages have disrupted the established global trade system. CSIS scholars provide analysis and commentary on the international trading system and its institutions.

Image

Photo: Sascha Schuermann/Getty Images

Restoring the Economics of Copper Processing

Copper processing economics are under pressure. Treatment and refining charges have turned negative as Chinese smelting capacity continues to outpace global mine supply, squeezing independent smelters worldwide and exposing the limits of current U.S. and allied policy responses.
